Kilohertz-Safe: A Scalable Framework for Constrained
Dexterous Retargeting
Yinxiao Tian∗, Ziyi Yang∗Zinan Zhao and Zhen Kan
Abstract— Dexterous hand teleoperation requires motion re-
targeting methods that simultaneously achieve high-frequency
real-time performance and enforcement of heterogeneous kine-
matic and safety constraints. Existing nonlinear optimiza-
tion–based approaches often incur prohibitive computational
cost, limiting their applicability to kilohertz-level control, while
learning-based methods typically lack formal safety guarantees.
This paper proposes a scalable motion retargeting framework
that reformulates the nonlinear retargeting problem into a
convex quadratic program in joint differential space. Hetero-
geneous constraints, including kinematic limits and collision
avoidance, are incorporated through systematic linearization,
resulting in improved computational efficiency and numerical
stability. Control barrier functions are further integrated to
provide formal safety guarantees during the retargeting process.
The proposed framework is validated through simulations and
hardware experiments on the Wuji Hand platform, outper-
forming state-of-the-art methods such as Dex-Retargeting and
GeoRT. The framework achieves high-frequency operation with
an average latency of 9.05 ms, while over 95% of retargeted
frames satisfy the safety criteria, effectively mitigating self-
collision and penetration during complex manipulation tasks.
I. INTRODUCTION
Dexterous teleoperation requires mapping high-
dimensional human hand motions to robotic hands under
strict real-time and safety constraints. In practical systems,
control commands must be generated at millisecond-level
latency to maintain responsiveness and closed-loop stability.
Meanwhile, dexterous robotic hands are mechanically
compact, with millimeter-scale clearances between fingers
and links, making them highly sensitive to numerical
errors, control delays, and constraint violations. Even small
deviations can result in self-collisions, actuator saturation,
or hardware damage. Consequently, motion retargeting for
dexterous manipulation must simultaneously support high-
frequency execution and strict enforcement of heterogeneous
constraints.
Existing dexterous hand retargeting methods generally
follow two paradigms. Optimization-based approaches, such
as DexPilot [1] and AnyTeleop [2], formulate retargeting
as constrained optimization problems that explicitly encode
kinematic consistency, joint limits, and motion smoothness.
These methods are interpretable and adaptable across dif-
ferent robotic hands, but typically rely on iterative nonlinear
solvers whose computational cost scales poorly with increas-

Anhui, China, 230026.ing degrees of freedom and constraint complexity, limiting
their ability to achieve stable kilohertz-level control.
Learning-based approaches address computational limi-
tations by shifting complexity to offline training. Recent
methods such as GeoRT [3] demonstrate that direct human-
to-robot mappings can achieve retargeting at 1 kHz with low
inference latency. However, such approaches are often tightly
coupled to specific robot embodiments and training datasets.
Safety constraints are usually enforced implicitly through
loss functions or heuristics, providing no formal guarantees.
As a result, performance can degrade in out-of-distribution
configurations or contact-rich scenarios, which restricts their
use in safety-critical manipulation tasks.
Formal safety and feasibility guarantees have been widely
studied in control and manipulation. In particular, Control
Barrier Functions (CBFs) provide a principled mechanism
for enforcing state and input constraints with theoretical
guarantees in real time [4]–[6]. However, integrating such
guarantees into high-frequency dexterous hand retargeting
remains challenging. Most existing retargeting pipelines rely
on heuristic collision penalties or offline nonlinear optimiza-
tion [7]–[12], and lack a unified, computationally efficient
framework for incorporating kinematic, geometric, and safety
constraints at kilohertz-level control rates.
To address this challenge, we propose Kilohertz-Safe, a
scalable dexterous teleoperation retargeting framework de-
signed from a system architecture perspective. Instead of
formulating retargeting as a standalone nonlinear optimiza-
tion or a purely learned mapping, Kilohertz-Safe introduces
a linearized control interface in joint differential space,
which enables heterogeneous constraints to be consistently
expressed and enforced under high-frequency control. Within
this unified formulation, safety is treated as a first-class
constraint rather than an auxiliary objective, and collision
avoidance is enforced with formal guarantees. The resulting
framework achieves computational efficiency suitable for sta-
ble millisecond-level control in high-dimensional dexterous
hand systems.
•We present Kilohertz-Safe, a scalable dexterous tele-
operation retargeting framework that reconciles high-
frequency real-time execution with heterogeneous con-
straint satisfaction, enabling stable millisecond-level
control for high-DoF robotic hands.
•We formulate safety specifications as explicit constraints
within a unified joint differential-space interface, pro-
viding formal guarantees of collision avoidance while
preserving computational efficiency.
•We validate the proposed framework through real-worldarXiv:2603.29213v1  [cs.RO]  31 Mar 2026

experiments on a dexterous hand platform, demonstrat-
ing its real-time performance and practical effectiveness
under safety-critical manipulation scenarios.
II. PRELIMINARIES
A. Dexterous Hand Retargeting
Dexterous hand retargeting aims to map human hand
motion to robot joint configurations such that the resulting
robot hand pose resembles the human hand pose while
respecting the kinematic limits of the robot. Due to the high
dimensionality of the hand and the morphological differences
between human and robot embodiments, this mapping is
commonly formulated as an optimization problem.
Specifically, geometric features such as fingertip positions
or joint keypoints are often used to characterize the hand
pose. Letvt

B. Control Barrier Functions
Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) [15] provide a princi-
pled way to enforce safety constraints in continuous-time
control systems. Given a system statex∈Rn, consider a
safety set
C={x|h(x)≥0},(2)
whereh(x)is a continuously differentiable function that
encodes safety constraints.
To ensure forward invariance of the safety set, a standard
CBF condition can be imposed on the system dynamics. For
first-order systems, this condition takes the form [6], [15]
˙h(x) +αh(x)≥0,(3)
whereα >0is a user-defined constant. This condition

incorporating formal safety guarantees into dexterous hand
retargeting systems.
III. METHOD
This section presents a retargeting framework for dexter-
ous hand teleoperation that enables stable and predictable
real-time execution at kilohertz control rates. Within this
framework, teleoperation mappings, geometric and kinematic
constraints, as well as safety-related constraints, although
inherently nonlinear in joint space, are locally linearized
around the current operating point and expressed as linear
equality and inequality constraints on joint velocities. This
unified formulation recasts dexterous-hand retargeting as a
structured convex optimization problem with bounded and
predictable computational complexity. As a result, the pro-
posed framework is well suited for high-frequency control
loops and remains scalable across dexterous hands with
different kinematic structures and degrees of freedom. The
remainder of this section details the individual components
of the framework and their practical implementation.

B. Control Barrier Function–Based Safety Guarantee
While the quadratic program in (7) enables task objectives
and physical constraints to be handled in a unified manner
under high-frequency control, it does not by itself guarantee
satisfaction of safety constraints throughout execution. Ex-
isting nonlinear optimization based retargeting approaches
typically encode collision avoidance by adding distance or
collision related penalties to the objective function. Such
treatments effectively impose soft constraints, whose safety
performance depends critically on heuristic weight tuning
and therefore can only mitigate collision risks in a prob-
abilistic or empirical sense, rather than providing formal
guarantees.
To enforce safety, we incorporate CBFs into the retargeting
formulation, yielding provable forward invariance of the safe
set during execution. Specifically, we construct a capsule-
based collision model in which robot links and environmental
obstacles are approximated by sets of geometric primitives.
For any potentially colliding pair of bodiesAandB, let
pA(q),p B(q)∈R3denote the closest (witness) points on
their respective skeletal segments. The corresponding safety
function is defined as
h(q) =∥p A(q)−p B(q)∥ 2−(r A+rB),(8)
wherer Aandr Bare the radii of capsulesAandB,
respectively. A collision occurs whenh(q)<0, and the safe

configuration set is given byS={q∈Rn|h(q)≥0}.
To guarantee forward invariance ofS, we impose the
condition ˙h(q)≥ −γh(q),whereγ >0controls the rate
at which the system is driven away from the safety bound-
ary. Enforcing this condition requires evaluating the time
derivative ofh(q), which can be obtained via differential
kinematics and Danskin’s Theorem. Let

Under high-frequency teleoperation, a first-order dis-

ing real-time solvability. In contrast, directly embedding
CBF constraints into a nonlinear retargeting formulation
would introduce high-dimensional nonlinear inequalities,
leading to prohibitive computational costs and rendering
high-frequency execution impractical.
IV. EXPERIMENT
A. Experimental Setup
We evaluate the proposed method in both simulation and
real-world experiments on the Wuji dexterous hand platform.
The simulation is conducted in the SAPIEN [21] environ-
ment using the official URDF model of the Wuji hand. Hu-
man hand keypoints are captured using a monocular laptop
camera and processed by the proposed retargeting pipeline to
output joint angles, which are executed directly in simulation.
This setup enables controlled evaluation of motion fidelity,
safety behavior, and computational performance.For hardware validation, the Wuji dexterous hand is
mounted on a fixed platform. Human hand motion is cap-
tured using an Intel RealSense camera, and hand keypoints
together with wrist poses are estimated in real time via
MediaPipe [22]. Both hand keypoints and wrist poses are
estimated in real time and retargeted to the robot hand,
demonstrating the applicability of the proposed framework
under practical sensing and actuation conditions.
We compare our approach against two representative
retargeting methods: Dex-Retargeting [2] and GeoRT [3],
under identical task setups and environmental conditions.
Performance is assessed using the following frame-wise
quantitative metrics.
1)Computation Latency:We evaluate computational ef-
ficiency by measuring the per-step latency of each
pipeline, defined as the wall-clock time required to
map a single human hand input frame to the cor-
responding robot joint targets. The reported latency
includes hand pose processing, retargeting computation,
and constraint-aware optimization, while excluding ren-
dering, visualization, and communication overhead.
Latency is recorded at each control step using system
timestamps. We report the mean, standard deviation, and
99th percentile across all trials. In addition, we report
the percentage of control steps that meet the target
control frequency, which reflects the real-time feasibility
of each method under a fixed control period.

B. Simulation Evaluation
We first evaluate different retargeting methods in the sim-
ulation environment. The evaluation covers motion preserva-
tion, collision safety, and real-time performance, and further
includes an ablation study to isolate the effect of explicit
safety constraints. For quantitative assessment, we report
computation latency, as well as the Motion Preservation and
Collision Safety Score introduced in Sec IV-A.
1) Computation Latency:Table I summarizes the real-
time performance comparison of three retargeting methods
on a simulated Wuji Hand platform. Owing to its unified
differential-space formulation, our approach achieves lower
average computation latency, reduced latency variability, and
a higher proportion of control steps satisfying the target con-
trol frequency. These results demonstrate that the proposed
system architecture enables stable millisecond-level retar-
geting under heterogeneous constraints. In contrast, GeoRT
exhibits higher computation latency, which is associated
with its reliance on geometric mapping operations and per-
frame heuristic corrections. Dex-Retargeting shows larger
latency fluctuations, as its optimization process exhibits
input-dependent computational complexity, leading to less
consistent real-time behavior.

3) Safety Analysis:Collision safety is critical for dexter-
ous hand retargeting, particularly during dense inter-finger
interactions. Fig. 4 plots the safety score over time with
key stages annotated; all methods are temporally aligned
for a fair comparison. Our approach consistently maintains
higher safety scores, whereas Dex-Retargeting and GeoRT
show sharp degradations during finger adduction and other
interpenetration-prone phases, due to the absence of explicit
collision-aware constraints. Quantitatively, more than 95%
of control steps achieve a safety score above 0.8, indicatingsustained collision clearance without sacrificing real-time
performance or motion fidelity.
To isolate the contribution of the explicit safety terms,
we perform an ablation that removes the safety terms while
keeping all other components unchanged. Under frame-
aligned tracking (the retargeted motion follows the human
input at each time step), Fig. 5(a) shows that the safety score
frequently drops below the prescribed threshold without
safety constraints, indicating elevated collision risk. Enforc-
ing the safety constraints, in contrast, yields consistently high
scores throughout the sequence.
We further analyze the induced physical safety behavior
by comparing the per-frame minimum inter-finger distance
(the minimum distance over all finger pairs) with and without
safety constraints (Fig. 5(b)). With safety constraints enabled,
the decrease in inter-finger distance is actively attenuated
as it approaches the safety threshold, effectively preventing
imminent collisions.
We set the minimum safety distance threshold to 0.01 m,
which defines the normalized safety score. The threshold is
selected according to the Wuji hand’s finger thickness and
joint clearances and is kept fixed across all experiments. To
account for system latency, we additionally introduce an acti-
vation distance that triggers the safety constraints in advance.

Finally, we qualitatively evaluate safety-constrained retar-
geting on representative gestures (Fig. 6). During grasping
(left), when the human fingers move into close or overlap-
ping configurations, safety constraints limit unsafe relative
motions between the corresponding robot fingers and prevent
geometric interpenetration; removing the constraints leads
to frequent self-collisions and severe penetration artifacts.
Similar issues occur during inter-finger contact (right): with-
out explicit safety constraints, interpenetration becomes pro-
nounced, while enforcing the constraints adaptively adjusts
joint motions to satisfy safety requirements while preserving
the overall gesture characteristics. Increasing the activation
distance further strengthens the preventive effect by interven-ing prior to contact.
C. Real-World Evaluation
In hardware experiments, we focus on qualitative evalua-
tion to assess real-world feasibility and motion naturalness. A
series of real-time human hand motions are tested, including
grasping and finger-crossing behaviors that are common
in daily manipulation and impose strict requirements on
responsiveness and collision avoidance. During evaluation,
we primarily examine the real-time responsiveness and safety
performance of the dexterous hand while executing contin-
uous motion sequences, validating the proposed framework
under practical sensing and actuation conditions.
The proposed framework maintains fixed-rate closed-loop
execution during hardware deployment, enabling consistent
control updates and continuous motion retargeting. The robot
hand smoothly follows human motions over extended contin-
uous sequences without observable control interruptions or
delay accumulation, indicating stable and reliable real-time
operation under practical sensing and actuation conditions,
as shown in Fig. 7.

To further evaluate execution safety during real-time op-
eration, we qualitatively compare the proposed framework
with Dex-Retargeting, and an ablation variant without the

As shown in Fig. 8, the baseline method may produce
configurations with reduced inter-finger clearance or unstable
finger interactions during challenging motions such as finger

hand configurations throughout execution, with no observ-

safety constraints effectively enable collision-aware motion
retargeting during real-world execution.
Overall, the hardware experiments validate the practical
deployability of the proposed framework in real-world en-
vironments. The presented motions cover diverse articula-
tion patterns including finger coordination, rapid posture
transitions, and large configuration changes, providing rep-
resentative evaluation scenarios for retargeting robustness.

V. CONCLUSIONS
This paper proposes a dexterous hand mapping framework
based on Convex Quadratic Programming, which enables
the efficient integration of heterogeneous constraints and
significantly enhances computational efficiency. By intro-
ducing Control Barrier Functions, the framework provides
theoretical safety guarantees, effectively eliminating self-
collision risks while preserving motion similarity. Future
research will explore the integration of tactile impedance
control constraints into the existing framework to optimize
torque distribution during object interaction and address the
issue of motor torque saturation.

structure.title: INTRODUCTION
structure.summary:
This partial document introduces "Kilohertz-Safe," a novel framework for dexterous hand teleoperation. The main points covered are:

*   **Problem Statement:** Existing methods for dexterous hand teleoperation struggle to simultaneously achieve high-frequency real-time performance (kilohertz-level control) and enforce complex kinematic and safety constraints. Nonlinear optimization methods are computationally expensive, while learning-based methods lack formal safety guarantees.
*   **Proposed Solution:** Kilohertz-Safe reformulates the nonlinear retargeting problem into a convex quadratic program in joint differential space. This approach linearizes heterogeneous constraints (kinematic limits, collision avoidance) for improved computational efficiency and numerical stability.
*   **Safety Guarantees:** Control barrier functions (CBFs) are integrated into the framework to provide formal safety guarantees during the retargeting process, treating safety as a first-class constraint.
*   **Validation and Performance:** The framework is validated through simulations and hardware experiments on the Wuji Hand platform. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods like Dex-Retargeting and GeoRT, achieving high-frequency operation with low latency and ensuring over 95% of retargeted frames satisfy safety criteria, effectively mitigating self-collision and penetration.
*   **Key Contributions:**
    *   A scalable framework that reconciles high-frequency execution with constraint satisfaction for high-DoF robotic hands.
    *   Formulation of safety specifications as explicit constraints within a unified joint differential-space interface, providing formal guarantees.
    *   Demonstration of real-time performance and practical effectiveness in safety-critical scenarios through real-world experiments.
*   **Technical Details:** The document outlines the quadratic programming formulation of hand pose retargeting using a first-order Taylor expansion of forward kinematics and introduces the concept of Control Barrier Functions for safety enforcement.

structure.title: PRELIMINARIES
structure.summary:
The partial document discusses a framework for dexterous hand teleoperation that aims to achieve real-time performance and safety in manipulation scenarios. It covers two main preliminary concepts:

1.  **Dexterous Hand Retargeting:** This section explains the goal of mapping human hand motion to robot hand joint configurations. It highlights that this is typically formulated as an optimization problem, using geometric features like keypoint positions to match human and robot hand poses while respecting robot kinematic limits. An example optimization problem is presented, balancing task-space tracking accuracy with temporal smoothness and joint limits.

2.  **Control Barrier Functions (CBFs):** This section introduces CBFs as a method for enforcing safety constraints in continuous-time control systems. It defines a safety set based on a continuously differentiable function and explains the condition required to ensure the system state remains within this safe set over time. For optimization-based control, the CBF condition is expressed as an inequality constraint on the control input, specifically as a linear constraint on joint velocities or increments, enabling real-time safety enforcement.

The document then proceeds to detail its proposed **Method**, which unifies teleoperation mappings, geometric, kinematic, and safety constraints into a structured convex optimization problem. This is achieved by locally linearizing nonlinear constraints around the current operating point and expressing them as linear constraints on joint velocities. The method is designed for high-frequency control loops and scalability across different dexterous hands. A key part of this method is the **Quadratic Programming Formulation of Hand Pose Retargeting**, which reformulates the nonlinear optimization problem into a quadratic program by using a first-order Taylor expansion of the forward kinematics.

nodes.title: Control Barrier Functions
nodes.summary:
This partial document describes a framework for dexterous hand retargeting in safety-critical manipulation scenarios. The main points covered are:

*   **Dexterous Hand Retargeting:** This section defines the problem of mapping human hand motion to robot hand configurations while respecting robot kinematic limits. It explains that this is typically formulated as an optimization problem using geometric features like keypoint positions and is often solved by minimizing the difference between human and robot keypoint positions, with added terms for temporal smoothness and joint limits.

*   **Control Barrier Functions (CBFs):** This section introduces CBFs as a principled method for enforcing safety constraints in continuous-time control systems. It explains how CBFs define a safety set using a continuously differentiable function and impose conditions on the system dynamics to ensure the state remains within this safe set. For optimization-based control, CBF conditions can be expressed as linear constraints on control inputs, such as joint velocities.

*   **Methodology (Unified Framework):** This section details a proposed retargeting framework designed for stable, predictable, real-time execution at high control rates (kilohertz). The core idea is to locally linearize teleoperation mappings, geometric, kinematic, and safety constraints around the current operating point, expressing them as linear equality and inequality constraints on joint velocities. This transforms the problem into a structured convex optimization problem with bounded computational complexity, making it suitable for high-frequency control loops and scalable to different dexterous hands.

*   **Quadratic Programming Formulation:** This part explains how the hand pose retargeting problem is reformulated as a convex quadratic program (QP). By applying a first-order Taylor expansion to the forward kinematics and expressing joint position limits as linear inequalities on joint differentials, the nonlinear optimization problem is converted into a standard QP form. This QP formulation is highlighted as a unified backbone for incorporating various constraints.

*   **CBF-Based Safety Guarantee:** This section addresses the limitations of traditional methods for safety constraint satisfaction (e.g., penalty-based approaches) and explains how CBFs are incorporated to provide provable forward invariance of the safe set. It describes constructing a capsule-based collision model and defining a safety function based on the distance between closest points on geometric primitives representing robot links and environmental obstacles.

structure.title: METHOD
structure.summary:
This partial document describes a high-frequency retargeting framework for robot teleoperation. The main points covered are:

1.  **Unified Constraint Linearization:** The framework linearizes high-frequency human input and robot state feedback at the velocity level to create a structured convex optimization problem. This includes linearization of teleoperation mapping, first-order kinematic linearization in joint-velocity space, and velocity-level affine constraints.
2.  **Geometric & Kinematic Constraints:** It incorporates linearized constraints for multi-degree-of-freedom dexterous hands, including distance and Jacobian-based constraints. Nonlinear distance constraints are transformed into linear ones.
3.  **Structured Convex Optimization:** The linearized constraints are fed into a convex optimization problem, specifically a quadratic program (QP). This QP formulation allows for unified handling of task objectives and physical constraints, including joint position limits rewritten as linear inequalities on joint differentials. The QP has a positive semi-definite Hessian, ensuring convexity and enabling real-time solutions.
4.  **Robot Motion Output:** The output of this optimization is the optimal joint update, leading to dexterous hand motion for the robot.
5.  **Safety Constraints (Control Barrier Function - CBF):** To provide formal safety guarantees, Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) are incorporated. This moves beyond probabilistic or empirical collision avoidance methods by ensuring provable forward invariance of the safe set. A capsule-based collision model is used, defining a safety function based on the distance between closest points on geometric primitives representing robot links and obstacles. A collision occurs when this safety function is negative.

nodes.title: Control Barrier Function–Based Safety Guarantee
nodes.summary:
The document describes a high-frequency retargeting framework for dexterous hand teleoperation. The main points covered are:

*   **Unified Constraint Linearization:** The framework unifies high-frequency human inputs and robot state feedback through velocity-level constraint linearization. This process transforms the original nonlinear retargeting problem into a structured convex optimization problem.
*   **Structured Convex Optimization:** The linearized constraints are incorporated into a convex quadratic program (QP). This QP formulation allows for the simultaneous handling of geometric, kinematic, and safety constraints, ensuring convexity and enabling real-time solutions.
*   **Geometric & Kinematic Constraints:** The framework addresses both nonlinear and linear distance constraints, as well as joint position limits, by rewriting them as linear inequality constraints on the joint differential.
*   **Safety Constraints (Control Barrier Function - CBF):** To provide formal safety guarantees, Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) are incorporated. This involves constructing a capsule-based collision model and defining a safety function. The CBF condition, expressed as $\dot{h}(q) \ge -\gamma h(q)$, is enforced through linear inequality constraints on the joint differential, ensuring forward invariance of the safe set.
*   **Robot Motion Output:** The optimal joint updates are computed through the QP, leading to dexterous hand motion.
*   **Experimental Setup and Evaluation:** The document details the experimental setup, including simulation in SAPIEN and real-world experiments with the Wuji dexterous hand. It also outlines the quantitative metrics used for evaluation: Computation Latency, Motion Preservation, and Collision Safety Score.
*   **Comparison with Existing Methods:** The proposed approach is compared against representative retargeting methods (Dex-Retargeting and GeoRT) to demonstrate its performance advantages.

structure.title: EVALUATION
structure.summary: The document discusses a method for dexterous hand teleoperation that ensures safety through forward invariance of a configuration set. It details the mathematical formulation for enforcing this safety condition using the time derivative of a distance function and point Jacobians. The approach discretizes these constraints into linear inequalities that can be incorporated into a convex quadratic program, enabling real-time solvability and formal geometric safety guarantees. The document then presents experimental evaluations in simulation and real-world scenarios using the Wuji dexterous hand platform. It compares the proposed method against two existing retargeting techniques (Dex-Retargeting and GeoRT) based on computational latency, motion preservation, and collision safety. The experimental results, including quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations, demonstrate the proposed method's advantages in terms of lower latency, improved motion fidelity, and robust safety performance.

nodes.title: Simulation Evaluation
nodes.summary:
The provided document excerpt details a simulation and real-world evaluation of a novel hand retargeting method. The main points covered are:

*   **Latency Comparison:** The proposed method ("Ours") demonstrates significantly lower mean latency, reduced latency variability (standard deviation), and a higher percentage of control steps meeting a 10ms target frequency compared to Dex-Retargeting and GeoRT. This is attributed to its unified differential-space formulation.
*   **Motion Preservation:** The proposed method achieves better motion preservation, meaning the retargeted robot hand motion more closely matches the human hand motion. This is quantified by cumulative motion preservation error and gain, with the proposed method showing consistently lower errors over time. Visualizations highlight its superior performance during critical interaction phases.
*   **Collision Safety:** The proposed method exhibits superior collision safety, maintaining higher safety scores throughout various hand gestures, especially during dense inter-finger interactions. This is achieved through explicit safety constraints, which prevent sharp degradations in safety scores seen in other methods. An ablation study confirms the effectiveness of these safety constraints (CBFs) in preventing self-collisions and maintaining inter-finger distances.
*   **Simulation Evaluation Summary:** The simulation evaluation covers motion preservation, collision safety, and real-time performance, including an ablation study to isolate the effect of safety constraints.
*   **Real-World Evaluation:** Hardware experiments focus on qualitative assessment of real-world feasibility and motion naturalness. The proposed framework demonstrates stable, reliable real-time operation with smooth motion following and no observable control interruptions. Qualitative comparisons with Dex-Retargeting and an ablation variant show that the proposed framework maintains safe hand configurations and prevents self-collisions during challenging real-world motions.
*   **Robustness and Generalization:** The method is shown to be robust across diverse human hand poses and generalizes well to a wide range of gestures.

nodes.title: Real-World Evaluation
nodes.summary:
The partial document describes a dexterous hand mapping framework that utilizes Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) for safety-constrained motion retargeting. Key points covered include:

*   **CBF Ablation Study:** Demonstrates that incorporating CBFs significantly improves collision safety scores and maintains a larger minimum inter-finger distance compared to methods without CBFs. Minor violations are attributed to discrete-time control and system latency.
*   **Proactive Collision Avoidance:** Explains how CBFs enable proactive collision avoidance by activating constraints when finger distances approach a predefined threshold, preventing collisions and penetrations even under latency.
*   **Qualitative Evaluation of Safety Constraints:** Compares grasping and inter-finger contact motions with and without safety constraints, showing that constraints effectively prevent self-collisions and geometric interpenetration. Increasing the activation distance leads to earlier intervention and more pronounced avoidance.
*   **Real-World Evaluation:** Assesses the framework's feasibility and motion naturalness in hardware experiments, focusing on real-time responsiveness and safety during grasping and finger-crossing motions. The framework demonstrates stable, real-time operation without observable control interruptions or delay accumulation.
*   **Comparison with Baseline Methods:** Qualitatively compares the proposed framework with Dex-Retargeting and a variant without QP-based safety constraints. The proposed method consistently maintains safe hand configurations and lower collision risk, preventing self-collisions during challenging motions.
*   **Conclusion:** Summarizes the framework's ability to achieve stable, fixed-rate closed-loop execution with safe hand configurations, enabling reliable, real-time, and safety-aware motion retargeting. Future work includes integrating tactile impedance control constraints.

structure.title: CONCLUSIONS
structure.summary: This partial document discusses a novel dexterous hand mapping framework that utilizes Convex Quadratic Programming for efficient integration of heterogeneous constraints and enhanced computational efficiency. A key feature of this framework is the incorporation of Control Barrier Functions, which provide theoretical safety guarantees by eliminating self-collision risks while maintaining motion similarity. The document also presents a qualitative comparison of collision risk during hand closing, showing that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches like Dex-retargeting and a variant without safety constraints. The authors conclude that their approach enables reliable, real-time, and safety-aware motion retargeting under practical conditions. Future research directions include integrating tactile impedance control constraints to optimize torque distribution and address motor torque saturation. The document also includes a comprehensive list of references related to hand retargeting, control barrier functions, and robotic manipulation.
